items.title: Captain Verne Streckfus Interview, 1960-09-22
items.q: Well, the first orchestra, we had a piano player and two pieces, three piece orchestra. He was a colored piano player, Charlie Mills, who we thought at that time was the finest piano player in the business.

ctx.x: And you personally, how long have you been aboard these boats? Ever since I was out of school. Ever since I was out of school. Of course, while I was in school, I was on them each summer. I made the summers on the boats. Do you mind if I ask your exact age? 65. And what is your birthday? July 27th. July 27th. So that would make you go on in 1895. 1895. 1895. See? And so you probably remember back from almost the very beginning yourself. First time. And his first time, yes. When these boats started, did they have…

Well, the first orchestra, we had a piano player and two pieces, three piece orchestra. He was a colored piano player, Charlie Mills, who we thought at that time was the finest piano player in the business. In later years, he went to foreign countries and he played a command performance before he came to England. Later returned to Chicago and very comfortably. He was born and raised in Quincy, Illinois. And when he died, which was about four or five years ago, he was returned to Quincy with honors as being an…

How many of your family are musical themselves? Well, we all play the instruments a little bit. Two brothers played the piano and two played the violin. Which two played the piano? Joe and John, and Roy and I played the violin. I see. So you know how to listen carefully to the music and judge the talent. Oh, we like music, yes. Who was playing with Charlie Mills? Do you remember the other two songs? The first name I don't know. That was the combination of piano, violin and drums. That was the first combination.…
